## Rationale

- **TOOL-306 CORE API** (Adopt): The single best surprise of the discovery sweep: works keyless from this container with real, large result sets, contradicting a plausible assumption that CORE needs a key. Directly answers the needs-table's 'which free keyed services would unblock discovery' question by showing CORE needs none. Also doubles as a full-text-access path (aggregates repository copies). Serves W1/W2 discovery and sub-task 3 (full-text access). Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.core.ac.uk/v3/search/works?q=pdf+repair&limit=1' -> HTTP 200, totalHits=4978068, 2026-09-27 (probe/core.json); CORE's own terms page confirms keyless access at 'one batch request or five single requests per 10 seconds' with no registration required
- **TOOL-300 Crossref REST API** (Adopt): Already the KB's main discovery+metadata backbone (used throughout research/sources/registry.jsonl). OBS-0600 shows it is the more complete of the two free forward-citation sources (0/10 zero-count sources vs OpenCitations' 5/10). Also answers sub-task 7: DOI to BibTeX/CSL via /works/<doi>/transform/<mime> works keyless, tested live. Serves W1/W2 discovery and P4 full review broadly; feeds forward-citation checks for any gap that depends on knowing whether a source has since been superseded or corroborated. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=pdf+repair&rows=1' -> HTTP 200, total-results=457305; works/<doi>, journals/<issn>/works and content-negotiation to application/x-bibtex all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-27 (see OBS-0600 and probe/crossref*.json, probe/das2018.bib)
- **TOOL-310 Unpaywall API** (Adopt): Confirms the needs-table's 'Unpaywall works keyless' state with a fresh, dated, first-hand test (previously only asserted, not independently re-verified this session). Correctly reports closed access for a known-closed IEEE paper, giving confidence in its accuracy. Directly serves sub-task 3 (full-text access) alongside CORE and direct PDF fetch. Evidence: python3 research/tools/polite_get.py 'https://api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1109/das.2018.64?email=research@pdfpundit.invalid' -> HTTP 200, {"is_oa":false,"oa_status":"closed",...}, 2026-09-27 (probe/unpaywall.json)
- **TOOL-421 radamsa** (Adopt): Builds cleanly from source with a tiny footprint (a few MB incl. its bootstrapped Ol/Owl Lisp interpreter); generic byte/structure-level mutation is a good coarse fault-injector but does not by itself reproduce DMG-009's specific *targeted* damage templates (offset corruption, xref corruption, stream-length mismatch, etc.) -- it would need to be paired with a format-aware wrapper (e.g. mutate only within object-stream boundaries) to do that. Evidence: git clone --depth 1 https://gitlab.com/akihe/radamsa.git (684KB) && make -j2 -> bin/radamsa, version string 'Radamsa 0.8a'. radamsa -s 1 sample_orig.pdf > mutated_radamsa.pdf: orig len 411513, mutated len 411596, 389954 bytes differing over the shared prefix. LICENCE confirmed MIT ('Copyright (c) 2013 Aki Helin ...'). See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-422 zzuf** (Adopt): Simple, fast, reproducible (seeded) random bit-flip injector -- a good match for the NAND-bit-flip-style DMG class (TOOL-407) specifically, complementing radamsa's more structural mutation style. Evidence: apt-installed; zzuf -s 0 -r 0.001 < sample_orig.pdf > mutated_zzuf.pdf: same size True, 3301 bytes differing (of 411513). Version and WTFPL copyright banner confirmed via `zzuf --version`. See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-402 digitalcorpora unsigned-S3 range-fetch technique** (Adopt): Confirmed fast and reliable; this is the working backbone for GAP-100's stratified sampler design, independent of the (currently blocked) CDX server and of data.commoncrawl.org's own reachability for the metadata half of the pipeline. Evidence: GET https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/?list-type=2&prefix=... returns S3 ListObjectsV2 XML (200 OK) with no credentials; range-fetching the first 2,000,000 bytes of corpora/files/CC-MAIN-2021-31-PDF-UNTRUNCATED/metadata/cc-provenance-20230303.csv.gz and decompressing via zlib.decompressobj(16+zlib.MAX_WBITS) yielded 12,946 usable CSV rows in 1.33s (OBS-0800); HEAD + central-directory read of a 1.66GB zip member (zipfiles/0000-0999/0001.zip) via HTTP range requests succeeded in 1.19s with 1 request, listing 1000 entries.
- **TOOL-352 PyMuPDF** (Adopt): Copyleft (AGPL): use out of process as a measurement tool, not in shipped code. Same per-class output as qpdf (OBS-0700); text ratio >= 0.95 of the original on 2/2 for C1, C2, C3, C6, C7, C8 and 0 on C9 and C10. Its page-1 text layer matched PDFium's exactly on all 19 sampled originals (OBS-0708). Renderer for SSIM/LPIPS against PDFium (OBS-0706, GAP-008). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.visual.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `pymupdf.open('<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2))` -> 6 pages, 9,221 text characters; textlayer_coverage.py ran 2026-10-05 on 19 originals (research/experiments/results/textlayer_coverage.csv, OBS-0708). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-464 fontTools** (Adopt): Serves GAP-003, GAP-205 and GAP-201 (OBS-0907, OBS-0906). Every Print to PDF font program keeps its real family name, although BaseFont is anonymous. Plan assumption changed: PR #16 and the plan treat Print to PDF fonts as nameless ('ignore the name'). Identity survives wherever a FontFile2 survives (C6, C9, partial C10). Name-free identification is needed only where no FontFile2 survives (C7/C8). Adopt for research-side analysis; the engine side needs a Rust reader (TOOL-465). Evidence: 2026-10-05: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout 600 nice -n 10 $S/venv/bin/python print_font_names.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf results/print_font_names` -> 'fontfile2_with_family_name': 889 of 889, 'parse_errors': 0, 'cmap_truth_agrees_with_tounicode': 35673 of 35792 (results/print_font_names.summary.json)
- **TOOL-426 pikepdf** (Adopt): Already known-good (qpdf-backed, permissive licence); confirmed again here as a reliable, fast sanity-check oracle for any newly generated or mutated PDF. Evidence: pikepdf.open(f) succeeded and reported the correct page count (1) for all 6 producer outputs in OBS-0801 (lo_input.pdf, sample_gs.pdf, sample_chromium.pdf, sample.pdf, sample_reportlab.pdf, sample_cairo.pdf). Version updated 2026-10-05 from the PyPI JSON API as reported by tooling-engines (report §7 item 2); 10.16.0 itself was not run in the container (10.14.0 was).
- **TOOL-418 pycairo (PDF surface)** (Adopt): Cairo is the rendering engine behind several real-world PDF producers (e.g. some GTK/Poppler-adjacent tools); dual-licensed LGPL/MPL, both permissive enough for this research-only use. Evidence: cairo.PDFSurface('sample_cairo.pdf', 200, 200); ctx.show_text(...); surface.finish() -> 7063 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-354 pypdfium2 (PDFium)** (Adopt): Rejects header damage (C1 0/2), otherwise as PyMuPDF (OBS-0700). Second renderer for SSIM/LPIPS: the MuPDF-vs-PDFium renderer floor on 19 originals is SSIM min 0.9039, median 0.9414 (OBS-0706), so visual scores must be computed within one renderer or against that floor (GAP-008). Repair route: open + save(); PDFium exposes no repair options. 5.14.0 untested. Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.visual.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `pypdfium2.PdfDocument('<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2))` -> 6 pages; `PdfDocument.save('pf.pdf')` -> 6-page output; textlayer_coverage.py ran 2026-10-05 (OBS-0708). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-417 reportlab** (Adopt): Produces very different, minimal-structure PDFs compared to office-suite/browser producers; useful for producer-diversity coverage at the opposite structural extreme. Evidence: canvas.Canvas(...).drawString(...); c.save() -> sample_reportlab.pdf, 1396 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-359 lopdf (Rust crate)** (Adopt): Adopt as a permissive Rust library and emitter, not as a strong repair baseline: load+save failed on C1, C4, C5 and C10 (0/2 each), the weakest loader on header and object-header damage (OBS-0700, DMG-250). Corroborates PR #16's note that lopdf needs a unique endstream and object headers at line start. Maintained (release 2026-09-08). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv, via experiments/rsprobe). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `rsprobe lopdf '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) l.pdf` -> 'lopdf ok pages=6 objects=165'. <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-373 jiwer** (Adopt): WER and a CER cross-check that matched rapidfuzz on every file (OBS-0704); WER complements CER for REPDF-style replication (GAP-008). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/cpr_step1_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.ocr.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: rv3.py, same pair as TOOL-372 -> 'jiwer WER 0.0'.
- **TOOL-372 rapidfuzz** (Adopt): CER (Levenshtein / reference length) agreed with jiwer on every CPR smoke file (OBS-0704) and with dinglehopper on all 8 OCR pages (OBS-0706). MIT and fast; replaces GPL python-Levenshtein (TOOL-381) (GAP-008). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results files research/experiments/results/cpr_step1_smoke.csv, research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.ocr.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: rv3.py in the scratch venv, PyMuPDF page-1 text of '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) vs '<REPDF>/original/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print).pdf' -> 'rapidfuzz 3.14.6 CER 0.0' (1,889 characters). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-375 scikit-image (SSIM)** (Adopt): The MuPDF-vs-PDFium floor on 19 originals is SSIM min 0.9039, median 0.9414, while damage gives C6 0.65-0.86 and C9 0.76-0.80 within one renderer (OBS-0706): score within one renderer and report both renderers (GAP-008, GAP-055). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/metrics_probe.visual.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: rv3.py, page 1 of '<REPDF>/original/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print).pdf' at 72 dpi gray, MuPDF vs PDFium -> 'skimage 0.26.0 SSIM mupdf-vs-pdfium p1 0.9398'. <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-415 Chromium headless print-to-pdf** (Adopt): Gives producer diversity plus indirect Skia coverage (Chromium's PDF export path uses Skia internally) without needing a separate Skia install. Evidence: /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome --headless --disable-gpu --no-sandbox --print-to-pdf=sample_chromium.pdf file://sample.html -> 25991 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). Harmless dbus/SSL-handshake stderr noise (no network/dbus socket in the sandboxed container) did not affect the output. See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-414 Ghostscript ps2pdf** (Adopt): Already apt-installed and used elsewhere in the project (gs 10.02.1, per stage2-tooling-needs.md); AGPL applies to Ghostscript itself, not to PDFs it produces, so producer-diversity use is unaffected, but redistributing any modified Ghostscript code would trigger AGPL. Evidence: ps2pdf sample.ps sample_gs.pdf -> 2477 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-416 LaTeX / pdflatex (texlive-latex-base)** (Adopt): A structurally distinct producer family (TeX's own PDF backend, not a general office/browser engine) that PDFPundit's REPDF-derived training data otherwise lacks. Evidence: pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -output-directory=... sample.tex -> sample.pdf, 16563 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). Installed texlive-latex-base (~35MB total incl. texlive-base dependency) for this check. See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-413 LibreOffice (soffice headless)** (Adopt): Works cleanly headless; a realistic, common real-world producer worth including in producer-diversity fixtures. Evidence: soffice --headless -env:UserInstallation=file://.../lo_profile --convert-to pdf lo_input.txt --outdir ... -> lo_input.pdf, 9929 bytes, opened by pikepdf (1 page). Required installing libreoffice-writer (~11MB; libreoffice-core alone fails silently on .txt input). See OBS-0801.
- **TOOL-368 infgen** (Adopt): Parsed all 54 Adler-only damaged streams to the trailer with unchanged block counts (damage confined to one block in 54), and named the DEFLATE fault in all 9 hard errors ('distance too far back', 'literal/length code is oversubscribed', ...) (OBS-0707). A cheap, permissive diagnostic for GAP-150/152; not a recovery tool. Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/deflate_tools_probe.csv; 63 damaged C9 streams). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `infgen -h` -> 'infgen 3.6'.
- **TOOL-323 PyMuPDF4LLM (pymupdf4llm)** (Adopt): The strongest hands-on result of this sweep: real heading structure plus a cleaner two-column read than either pdfplumber or the existing pdftotext baseline, directly useful for isolating a paper's Conclusion/Limitations text for sub-task 5. Its AGPL-3.0-or-later licence (the free option of the dual licence) is copyleft: fine for this research pipeline's own internal use (we are not distributing it or linking it into the PDFPundit product, which is the pure-Rust/lopdf-only artifact under the charter's clean-room rule), but flag it clearly so no one later vendors its output-generation code into the shipped tool. Evidence: OBS-0601: pip-installed into a scratch venv (369 MB total with pdfplumber, deleted after) and run on the cached CPR PDF: converted to Markdown in 7.9s, correctly leveled every section heading (Introduction..Conclusion), located '### References' as its own heading with individually separated entries, and stayed column-clean at the same two-column boundary where pdfplumber and pdftotext both garbled the text; 2026-09-27
- **TOOL-356 Apache PDFBox (pdfbox-app jar)** (Adopt): Text on C1-C9 like PyMuPDF except 1/2 on C8 at ratio >= 0.95 (OBS-0700). Best-of from the jar's own help: decode (writedecodeddoc: writes the document with all streams decoded, the rewrite/repair route) and export:text. Permissive and maintained (GAP-009). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05: `java -jar pdfbox-app-3.0.8.jar export:text -i='<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) -o=pb.txt` -> exit 0, 12,363 bytes (warning 'No Unicode mapping for CID+496'); `java -jar pdfbox-app-3.0.8.jar decode '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2) pbd.pdf` -> exit 0, 6-page output (warning 'Did not found XRef object at specified startxref position 0'). <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-358 Ghostscript (gs pdfwrite, txtwrite)** (Adopt): Copyleft (AGPL): binary only. txtwrite matched PyMuPDF's per-class output; one 60 s timeout on a C9 file (OBS-0700). It repairs by default and -dPDFSTOPONERROR is the strict control (CLM-0705). Header loss needs the PDF interpreter forced, or gs reads the file as PostScript (OBS-0501, GAP-256). Best-of: -sDEVICE=pdfwrite re-distill and txtwrite, with PDF forced when the header is gone (GAP-009). Evidence: ran 2026-09-27 (results file research/experiments/results/engine_smoke.csv). Re-checked 2026-10-05 after rebuilding the conda-forge env (deleted after the check): `gs -q -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -o gw.pdf -sDEVICE=pdfwrite '<REPDF>/corrupted/print/text/Next_Decade_Space_Exploration(print)_xref.pdf' (C2)` -> exit 0, 6-page output; `-sDEVICE=txtwrite` -> 16,415 bytes; `-dPDFSTOPONERROR -o /dev/null -sDEVICE=nullpage` -> exit 1, 'Error: /syntaxerror in --runpdf--'. <REPDF> = /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf @ e547d4d.
- **TOOL-351 MuPDF mutool (clean, draw)** (Adopt): Copyleft (AGPL): run as a separate binary only, never link or copy code (clean-room rule). The only engine with output on C4 (2/2) and C5 (2/2), but its C4 outputs keep 1 page, so 'produced output' is not fidelity (OBS-0700); no output on C10. Best-of option set from pdfclean.c's usage text (CLM-0704, SRC-0501): clean -gg, clean -gggg, clean -gggg -s (sanitize content streams); -d decompresses for inspection.
